# Reliable Text-to-SQL with Adaptive Abstention

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#rts)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.10858v1) · arXiv:2501.10858v1, 18 January 2025 author manuscript; ACM DOI 3709719 identified in manuscript

**Reading coverage:** All substantive Sections 1–6 on pages 1–14 of the 17-page manuscript, Theorems 1-3 and proofs, Algorithms 1-2, Tables 1-9 and figures/captions. Remaining pages are references; no appendices.

## Research question

Schema-linking models can make confident token errors that propagate into SQL; raw token confidence is insufficient for the studied fine-tuned model.

## Method

Teacher-forced traces locate branching tokens; layer-specific hidden-state classifiers and conformal prediction sets detect them. Aggregation triggers abstention, a surrogate relevance check or human correction before downstream SQL generation.

## Evaluation

BIRD and Spider schema-linking and execution metrics with fine-tuned DeepSeek/CodeS models; 20 student participants evaluate 100 sampled questions across expertise levels. The theory concerns marginal prediction-set coverage under calibration assumptions.

## What the results support

Abstention raises linking accuracy among retained cases; human assistance recovers high linking accuracy and improves downstream execution. A surrogate reduces interventions but admits additional errors. Beginners perform worse on difficult column decisions.

## Limits and qualifications

Requires hidden-state access, task-specific labels and a compatible calibration distribution; drift is outside experiments. Human-assisted linking is not autonomous SQL reliability. The draft has reporting inconsistencies: downstream 65.19% is assigned to DeepSeek in prose but CodeS-15B in Table 7, and TAR/FAR formulas reverse the prose conditions.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Important abstention-at-schema-linking design with bounded statistical claims, not a correctness guarantee for full generated SQL or unknown-intent resolution.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| DeepSeek-7B reaches 65.19% execution accuracy. | Table 7 assigns 64.72% to DeepSeek RTS-schema and 65.19% to CodeS-15B, contrary to Section 4.3 prose. | Section 4.3 p. 11 and Table 7 p. 12 | Use table-specific model attribution; avoid repeating prose value. |
| The printed TAR/FAR formulas implement their descriptions. | TAR prose describes incorrect generations but formula uses equality; FAR prose describes correct generations but formula uses inequality. | Section 4.2 p. 10 | Metric-expression inconsistency; do not translate those formulas into new factual claims. |
